# What this book is {.unnumbered}

This book is the guide to **ISLA** (Invariant Slice Attention), a neural
surrogate for steady, boundary-driven PDE problems. Given a discretized
boundary and the problem's global conditions, ISLA predicts the steady field
on that boundary and in the domain it bounds. The book is written the way a
user guide for a design code is written. It teaches what the method computes
and why each part is there. It shows how to run it. Then it lays out, with
the same care, what the measurements say for it and against it. The reader
we have in mind is fluent in PDE numerics and machine learning and has never
seen this program. Every term is defined where it first appears. Every
number is computed from a checked-in artifact as the page renders.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Where the name comes from"}
An *isla* is an island, a shape defined entirely by its boundary. The boundary is what the method takes as input.
The code class is `physicsnemo.experimental.models.ISLA`.
:::

## The thesis {#sec-verdict}

**ISLA is a slice-attention surrogate that is exactly equivariant to rigid
motions and consistent under a change of boundary discretization, and it
pays nothing in accuracy for either.** The two invariances are defined in
@sec-invariances. It is measured against GeoTransolver, the strongest
published slice-attention surrogate, and Transolver, with every model
given the same inputs and scored on the same instrument at the reporting
protocol of @sec-protocol. Where the evaluation departs from the training
conventions, in pose or in how the surface was sampled, ISLA's error
barely moves and the baselines' error grows by factors; in distribution it
leads GeoTransolver at the recipe width on the cars, ties the parameter
match at lower cost, and trails on the wings and on tensor targets.
@tbl-thesis is the standing, one row per dataset and task.

```{python}
#| label: setup-index
#| include: false
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
RES = Path("..") / "results"
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
mean = statistics.mean

# ISLA is the reference configuration (384 x 12, cosine routing, fused kernel, 5e-4): results/ref_surface_2026-09-23.json
REF = J("ref_surface_2026-09-23.json")["summary"]
refm = lambda k, f="pressure_l2": REF[k]["fields"][f]["mean"]
# DrivAerML Surface task, 435 cars, the reporting protocol: GeoTransolver-256 and Transolver at their better learning rate
P2 = J("p200k_trio_reduction_2026-09-19.json")["arms"]
isla200 = refm("isla_r1|dr435"); t200 = P2["transolver_unit_lr3e3"]["pressure_mean"]; gt512 = refm("gt_w512|dr435")
_gts = {k: P2[k]["pressure_mean"] for k in ("gt_unit_lr1e3", "gt_unit_lr3e3") if P2[k]["pressure_mean"]}
gt200_key = min(_gts, key=_gts.get); gt200 = _gts[gt200_key]; gt200_lab = "3e-3" if gt200_key.endswith("3e3") else "1e-3"
CSW = {r["arm"]: r for r in J("cost_sweep_ref_gb300_bf16_2026-09-22.json")["runs"] if r["tokens"] == 200000 and r["status"] == "ok"}
memx = lambda a: CSW[a]["peak_allocated_gib"] / CSW["isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused"]["peak_allocated_gib"]
stepx = lambda a: statistics.median(CSW[a]["step_ms"]) / statistics.median(CSW["isla_ref_r1_384x12_cos_fused"]["step_ms"])
# DrivAerML Surface task, the training-car ladder at the reporting protocol
RBS = J("refboard_ladder_2026-09-23.json")["summary"]
lad200 = {n: min(RBS[f"gt256|n{n}"]["mean"], RBS[f"gt256_lr3e3|n{n}"]["mean"]) / RBS[f"isla_r1|n{n}"]["mean"] for n in (27, 54, 109, 218)}
# HiLiftAeroML case rungs against the parameter-matched GeoTransolver-512
import glob as _glob
def ref_lane_seeds(stem, f="pressure_l2"):
    out = []
    for sd in (42, 43):
        fs = sorted(_glob.glob(str(RES / "campaigns_2026-09-22" / "ref" / "metrics" / f"{stem}_seed{sd}" / "**" / "metrics.jsonl"), recursive=True))
        rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(fs[0]) if '"infer_step"' in l]
        out.append(mean(r["metrics"][f] for r in rows))
    return out
SLW = J("scalelaw_2026-09-27.json")["configurations"]
wing = {35: refm("gt_w512|hl35") / refm("isla_r1|hl35"),
        210: mean(ref_lane_seeds("ref_gt_w512_hl210")) / mean(ref_lane_seeds("ref_isla_r1_hl210")),
        510: mean(SLW["hilift|gt|w512|n510"]["pressure_l2_seeds"]) / mean(ref_lane_seeds("ref_isla_r1_hl510"))}
# the solids, GeoTransolver-512 (the parameter match) ÷ ISLA
LUGR = J("solids_lug_2026-09-22.json")["gt512_over_isla"]
lug = {300: LUGR["isla_r1_lr25e4|n300"], 600: LUGR["isla_r1|n600"], 1200: LUGR["isla_r1|n1200"], 2400: LUGR["isla_r1|n2400"]}
_LM = J("lane_means_2026-09-23.json"); _SFG = J("solids_frame_2026-09-22.json")["summary"]["gt512|gt|n400"]["fields"]
T2 = {f: _SFG[f]["mean"] / mean(_LM[f"v2_t2d_isla_r1_tensor_axis_n400_seed{s}"]["fields"][f] for s in (42, 43)) for f in ("sig11", "sig22", "sig12", "displacement")}
JBS = J("deepjeb_2026-09-22.json")["summary"]
jb_full = {f: JBS["gt256|full"]["fields"][f]["mean"] / JBS["isla_r1|full"]["fields"][f]["mean"] for f in ("von_mises", "displacement")}
JBR = J("deepjeb_2026-09-22.json")["gt512_over_isla"]
# every case in a random pose, DrivAerML Surface task at the reporting protocol
PP = J("p200k_pose_r1_2026-09-23.json")
pose = {"isla": PP["arms"]["isla"]["posed_over_native"], "gt": PP["arms"]["gt_unit"]["posed_over_native"], "t": PP["arms"]["transolver_unit"]["posed_over_native"]}
pose_lead = {"gt": PP["verdict"]["gt_aug_posed_over_isla_posed"], "t": PP["verdict"]["t_aug_posed_over_isla_posed"]}
# the 10:1 biased inference draw on the 35-wing rung, every model at 200,000 cells
CR = J("consistency_r1_2026-09-23.json")["arms"]; WB = J("wingbench_200k_reduction_2026-09-19.json")["arms"]
bias = {"isla": CR["isla_r1_hl35_200k"], "gt": WB["gt_unit_lr3e3"], "t": WB["transolver_unit"]}
bfac = lambda a: a["mean"]["biased"] / a["mean"]["unif"]
# the two interior tasks against GeoTransolver-volume
FIELDS = ("pressure_l2", "velocity_l2", "nut_l2")
VG = J("ratevol_reduction_2026-09-20.json")["arms"]["gt_vol_unit"]
vol_ratio = {f: VG[f]["mean"] / refm("isla_r1|drvol", f) for f in FIELDS}
AF = J("airfrans_reduction_2026-09-22.json")["arms"]["gt_volume_1e-3"]
af_ratio = {f: AF[f]["mean"] / refm("isla_r1|af", f) for f in FIELDS}

def standing(r, names=("pressure", "velocity", "eddy viscosity")):
    """Word a triple of baseline ÷ ISLA ratios: above 1.02 ISLA leads, below 0.98 it trails, else level."""
    lead = [n for n, f in zip(names, FIELDS) if r[f] > 1.02]; trail = [n for n, f in zip(names, FIELDS) if r[f] < 0.98]
    level = [n for n, f in zip(names, FIELDS) if 0.98 <= r[f] <= 1.02]
    parts = []
    if lead: parts.append("ISLA leads on " + " and ".join(lead))
    if trail: parts.append("trails on " + " and ".join(trail))
    if level: parts.append("level on " + " and ".join(level))
    return "; ".join(parts)
```

```{python}
rows = [

     " / ".join(f"{lug[n]:.2f}" for n in (300, 600, 1200, 2400)) + f"; {jb_full['von_mises']:.2f} / {jb_full['displacement']:.2f}",
     f"ISLA leads where the target is a frame-free scalar, at the two small lug rungs ({lug[300]:.2f} and {lug[600]:.2f}) and at every DeepJEB++ rung",

     "GeoTransolver-512 leads on every component; the open standing of the book",
     "@sec-interior-tensile2d"),
    ("**Pose and sampling draw** at 200,000 cells: every case in its own random pose (DrivAerML Surface, baselines rotation-augmented, ISLA not); error under a 10:1 front/back biased draw ÷ under the uniform draw (HiLiftAeroML, 35 wings)",
     f"{pose_lead['gt']:.2f} / {pose_lead['t']:.2f}; ISLA {bfac(bias['isla']):.2f}x against {bfac(bias['gt']):.1f}x and {bfac(bias['t']):.1f}x",
     f"ISLA's own error moves {pose['isla']:.3f}x between native and posed evaluation where the baselines' moves {pose['gt']:.2f}x and {pose['t']:.2f}x, and it is unchanged under the biased draw",
     "@sec-pose-contract, @sec-robustness-density"),
]
out = "| Dataset, task and setting | baseline ÷ ISLA | Reading | Chapter |\n|---|---:|---|---|\n"
for r in rows: out += "| " + " | ".join(r) + " |\n"
print(out)
print(f": The thesis in {len(rows)} rows, one dataset and task per row. "
      "How to read this: each row is one setting and one instrument, so rows are not comparable with one another, and a ratio is the named "
      "baseline's error divided by ISLA's, so a value above one favors ISLA. "
      "ISLA is the reference configuration throughout (384 wide, 12 layers, cosine routing, the fused geometry kernel, learning rate 5e-4, "
      "@sec-using-config), and the setting is the reporting protocol of @sec-protocol unless the row says otherwise. "
      "Errors are the area-weighted relative L2 (@sec-metrics) in float32, seed means over two seeds, of surface pressure on the surface "
      "tasks and of the named fields elsewhere. "
      "The seeds, the paired counts and the controls behind each row, and the `results/` artifact each number is computed from, are in the "
      "chapter the row cites. {#tbl-thesis}")
```

## How to read this book {#sec-how-to-read}

**The book reads in order. Each chapter assumes only the ones before it.**

- **The problem and how we measure** (@sec-problem): the boundary-to-field
  operator and its general interface, taught on a two-dimensional airfoil
  whose exact solution we know, then the generalization axes, the metric
  and the instrument.
- **ISLA, one idea at a time** (@sec-isla): why each part of the
  architecture is there, from "a sum over cells should be an integral" to
  the equivariant output basis.
- **The two invariances ISLA is built for** (@sec-invariances): what
  rigid-motion equivariance and discretization consistency mean, what each
  buys, and every pose and discretization measurement of the book.
- **The ISLA forward pass** (@sec-architecture): the computation stage by
  stage, with every tensor shape and code identifier.
- **Baselines, datasets and the protocol** (@sec-baselines): GeoTransolver
  and Transolver, the dataset roster and the conventions they share, and
  the rules that make a comparison fair.
- **Using ISLA** (@sec-using): the reference configuration, the inputs, the
  commands, the sampler, checkpoints and cost.
- **Evidence, by dataset.** One chapter per dataset, each in the same
  order: the problem and its diversity, what is measured, the standing of
  the three architectures, the ladders and controls, and what the dataset
  does not say. DrivAerML, both tasks (@sec-drivaerml); HiLiftAeroML
  (@sec-hilift); AirfRANS (@sec-airfrans); Shift-SUV (@sec-shift-suv);
  PLAID Tensile2d (@sec-tensile2d); the GINOT bracket lug (@sec-lug);
  DeepJEB++ (@sec-deepjeb). Then capacity, scaling laws and cost
  (@sec-capacity), the one evidence chapter organized by question rather
  than by dataset.
- **Limits and open questions** (@sec-limits), then **program status**
  (@sec-program-status), the one chapter with dates.
- **Appendices.** The names and colors and the design-decision ledger
  (@sec-principled-decisions), ISLA against the literature
  (@sec-isla-vs-geotransolver), and the lab notebook (@sec-notebook): every
  preregistration, launch and verdict, including the failures, in the order
  they happened.

Every claim's scope is in @sec-limits, which also says what the book does
not claim.

Optional depth sits in collapsed notes like the one at the top of this
page. The throughline reads completely with all of them closed.
